subject: Follow-up: Finovate incident — deployment path & expedited onboarding
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finovate.ai>, Samir Desai <samir.desai@finovate.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & immediate ask — incident-driven capacity need

Hi Priya / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps while the incident is still fresh for both teams.

What we heard from your ops team
- Sudden spike in inference traffic during a marketing event caused a 7–8x increase in concurrent sessions.
- Hosted routes hit throttles and some requests fell back to lower-priority pools, increasing latency beyond your SLO.
- You have strict data residency and audit requirements for the payment flows.

Immediate asks / constraints
1) Timeline: you need an operational mitigation within 48–72 hours and a more durable fix within 10 business days.
2) Security: any private deployment must include KMS integration and audit-log export.
3) Procurement: your procurement lead indicated a short window to approve a committed capacity PO if we provide accelerated onboarding and a short-term credit.

Recommended short plan (high level)
A — Short-term (0–72h): enable burst capacity on Dedicated (reserved GPUs) and apply a temporary routing policy to divert payment-critical traffic to the dedicated pool. This is the fastest way to stop throttles while preserving Hosted for non-critical paths.
B — Medium-term (7–10 business days): spin up a Private VPC trial for payment flows with KMS + audit logging configured; run a staged cutover (canary) for the highest-volume endpoints.
C — Long-term: evaluate full migration for payment workloads or a hybrid model (Hosted for general traffic + Private for regulated flows).

Attachments included: incident-screenshots.png (ops logs), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (initial timeline & owners), soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 summary we can share while we run the security review).

Next steps I propose now
- Marcus: can you confirm feasibility of a 48–72h burst-to-dedicated path and list exact infra prerequisites?
- Ben: I can loop procurement on your side; Ben, can you draft a short-term offer (capacity + credit) we can escalate?
- Priya / Samir: please send the procurement contact and any internal compliance checklist items we should prioritize.

I’ll schedule a 30-min working call for 10:30 PT today unless someone suggests a different time.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0189
--
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finovate.ai>, Samir Desai <samir.desai@finovate.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & immediate ask — incident-driven capacity need

Tessa / team —

Thanks for the clear framing. Short answers up front: yes, feasible — we can implement a burst-to-dedicated mitigation within ~48 hours assuming the customer approves a short-term reserved capacity and we get networking details. A few specifics and caveats: 

What I need from Finovate to hit 48–72h
- VPC peering CIDR (if they want dedicated in VPC) or public IP allowlist for dedicated control-plane comms.
- KMS provider and key alias (if they require customer-managed keys for the canary).
- A contact on the infra team with SSH access for initial validation (or we can do a pre-approved runbook step-by-step).

Technical approach (phased)
1) Provision a small dedicated GPU pool with autoscale headroom and a dedicated routing policy scoped to payment endpoints.
2) Apply continuous batching/kv-cache tuning for those endpoints to reduce token cost under heavy concurrency.
3) Start a canary route for the 5 highest-volume URLs and monitor 95th/99th latency and error rate.

Operational notes
- We can enable rollback to Hosted automatically on error.
- Burst capacity will incur a short window of increased cost; I’ll put numbers in the MAP.

I attached a short checklist for infra (I’ll paste it into the MAP). If Priya / Samir can provide the two items above by EOD, we can start provisioning tomorrow.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
--

Tessa / Marcus / Finovate —

I can prepare a short-term reserved capacity offer with an onboarding credit to make the initial 48–72h move economical. Proposed commercial accelerators:
- 2-week trial reserved pool (min commitment) with a one-time onboarding credit offsetting first invoice by 40%.
- Option to convert the trial into a 3-month reserved contract at a pre-agreed rate to cover the medium-term need.

To move fast I need the procurement contact and a PO contact. If Finovate can sign a 1–2 page acceptance for the trial (we can send an expedited SOW), we can queue provisioning in <24h from signature.

Also looping Laura for security checklist items that may impact the timeline (KMS, audit log endpoints, SOC 2 evidence).
